CP-0.analysis_md:
The Source Pack supports the Distressed & Restructuring work for Larchmere Leisure Group, Inc. (fictional) with limitations: 8 issuer files, one market file and two portfolio files were classified, all readable and all naming the right entity [C1]. The pack holds the credit agreement as amended, the notes indenture, the master-lease summary, the late compliance certificate and the non-payment notice, which are the documents a restructuring read needs. Market evidence is a single dealer file dated 1 October 2026 [C2].

The pack has no rating-agency report: ratings come from the market file only, so the rating-trigger module cannot establish agency thresholds and is expected to be Blocked. The Source Pack also lacks an independent valuation and any lender-group intercreditor term sheet, so enterprise values rest on analyst multiples. One portfolio was found, Fenwick Park CLO Ltd (fictional), holding a single position in the first-lien loan [C3]. Two Deep Research questions were offered and not approved; no earlier Report was found.

CP-1.analysis_md:
The canonical record shows a company whose cash earnings no longer cover its fixed charges. LTM net revenues to 30 June 2026 are 1,412 against 1,492 in FY2025 [C1], and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA is 210 against 241 in FY2025; first-half Adjusted EBITDA fell 25.0% to 93 [C2]. Face debt at 30 June 2026 is 1,700, so total leverage on the company's EBITDA is 8.10x (calc: total leverage on face debt = 1,700 / 210 = 8.10x); the revolver is fully drawn at 200 [C14]. USD millions throughout; confidence is Restricted.

Cash flow is the sharper signal. Operating cash flow was 14 in FY2025 and -21 in H1 2026, and capital spending was 21 in the half [C8][C9], so LTM free cash flow is -67 (calc: LTM free cash flow = (-21) + (-46) = -67). Cash interest of 147 LTM and master-lease cash rent of 62 [C5][C6] absorb all of the company's 210 of Adjusted EBITDA. Unrestricted cash is 62 [C13].

Reported EBITDA is Adjusted EBITDA less three add-backs; the bridge closes in every period. Run-rate cost savings of 16 LTM are announced but not delivered and are carried as NOT_STATED for CP-1D to rule on [C12]. Segment revenue shows the mix: Gulf Coast fell 11.4% and Mid-South 11.6% in H1 2026 on H1 2025, and Online 3.5% [C18]. The master-lease financing obligation of 1,149 stays outside debt [C16]. Facility terms and balances are in the debt register [C15].

CP-1A.analysis_md:
The facts that matter most to a creditor are the rent burden, the sponsor's lack of committed support and the missed coupon. Larchmere is a sponsor-owned regional casino operator with eleven properties in four states, seven of them on one master lease and four owned [C2]. Its ratings are Caa2 (negative) from Moody's since 21 July 2026 and CCC (negative) from S&P since 4 August 2026 [C4].

Revenue is concentrated: Gulf Coast is 48.5% and Mid-South 39.4% of LTM revenue, with Online at 12.1% [C6]. The sponsor holds 88% of the equity and has committed no support [C3], and the landlord holds consent and cross-default rights over any restructuring.

The event sequence shows a company moving from a covenant reset in June 2025 to a missed coupon on 15 September 2026, a late compliance certificate showing a leverage breach on 21 September and a sponsor proposal for 150 of priming new-money debt on 22 September [C5]. Confidence in this module is Medium; every fact is from the company's own documents, which a Restricted pack cannot corroborate.
CP-1A.gaps_md:
- Morningstar issuer id and Fitch rating: none in the pack. Effect: blank cells in the profile. Lifted by: a Morningstar export.
- Management biographies, tenure and compensation: not in the pack. Effect: governance view is limited to ownership and lease terms. Lifted by: the proxy-style disclosure in the annual report.
- Competitor supply by market: not in the pack; the loss-of-share claim rests on the company's own statistics. Lifted by: Deep Research (not approved) or a gaming-board market report.

rows: Dana Whitcombe (CEO, fictional); Rafael Okonkwo (CFO, fictional)

Larchmere operates eleven casino resorts in Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri and Indiana plus an online sports-betting and iGaming business, serving mainly drive-in regional customers. Gaming is the large majority of revenue; hotel, food and entertainment are supporting lines. Seven of the eleven properties are leased from one landlord under a single master lease; four are owned.
Gulf Coast 48.5%, Mid-South 39.4% and Online 12.1% of LTM revenue.
Two drive-in regional markets carry almost 90% of revenue and both are losing share to new competitors.
Revenue stabilisation depends on Gulf Coast, where hotel occupancy has fallen from 87% to 77%.

[C6] calc: seg_gulf_coast share of LTM revenue = 685 / 1412 * 100 = 48.5% calc: seg_mid_south share of LTM revenue = 556 / 1412 * 100 = 39.4% calc: seg_online share of LTM revenue = 171 / 1412 * 100 = 12.1%
7 of 11 properties are leased from Brightwater Gaming Properties Trust (fictional) under one master lease; cash rent is 62 LTM with a 1.5% escalator.
Rent is a fixed claim that ranks ahead of funded creditors in practice and cross-defaults with the funded debt.
The lessor is a pivotal party in any restructuring, and rent shrinks distributable value in every scenario.
About 58% of gaming revenue comes from rated loyalty-programme players; gaming is 71% of revenue.
A discretionary, drive-in customer base trades down quickly when real incomes fall.
EBITDA is cyclical and operating deleverage is high, so a revenue decline of about 11% removes roughly a quarter of EBITDA.
Online (sports betting and iGaming) is 12% of revenue and about 192 thousand monthly active players, flat to down on a year ago.
A sub-scale online arm without a growth case consumes marketing spend and adds little to cash flow.
Online has limited value in a sale and sits in a subsidiary that can be designated unrestricted, so it is a drop-down candidate.
Quillon Ridge Partners (fictional) holds 88% and appoints four of seven directors, four appointed by the sponsor; no equity support is committed.
Support depends on a negotiation; the equity cure is available but the sponsor has not committed to use it.

Under the master lease, an event of default under the funded debt that is not cured within 30 days is an event of default under the master lease, and the landlord must consent to a change of control and to any assignment of the lease in a restructuring.
A funded-debt default can accelerate the lease, so the landlord holds a veto over any out-of-court or court path.

CP-1D.analysis_md:
92.4% of the company's 210 Adjusted EBITDA is supported by the evidence: SSIM EBITDA is 194 after rejecting the 16 of run-rate savings [C3] (calc: share of stated EBITDA supported = 194 / 210 * 100 = 92.4%). If the restructuring costs are treated as recurring, as the three-year pattern suggests, the supported figure falls to 172 (calc: EBITDA if restructuring costs are recurring = 194 - 22 = 172). The sponsor fee is realized and contractual. Confidence is Medium.

Cash conversion is the weakest part of earnings quality: operating cash flow was a fifth of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2024 and is negative LTM [C4][C5]. The company's EBITDA no longer funds its interest and rent.

Beyond face debt, the debt-like items are 44.25 (an accrued unpaid coupon, an earn-out and a pension withdrawal liability) [C6]. Adjusted debt is 1,744.25 (calc: adjusted debt = 1,700 + 44.25 = 1,744.25) and adjusted leverage 8.99x (calc: adjusted leverage = 1,744.25 / 194 = 8.99x). The master-lease financing obligation of 1,149 is deliberately outside these figures and sits in the Model's lease-adjusted lines.
CP-1D.gaps_md:
- Savings programme detail: the company gave no plan, headcount or closure schedule behind the 16 of run-rate savings. Effect: the savings cannot be tested, so they are rejected. Lifted by: the management plan.
- Quarterly cash conversion: only half-year cash flows are reported. Lifted by: quarterly cash-flow statements.

CP-2.analysis_md:
Larchmere is a Stressed credit on a Deteriorating direction in a Negative sector. The strongest support is hard assets: four owned properties and eleven licences with an appraised value of 1,180 [C14]. The primary downside is that cash earnings no longer cover fixed charges: SSIM EBITDA of 194 meets 209 of cash interest and rent, a cover of 0.93x (calc: fixed-charge cover = 194 / 209 = 0.93x) [C1][C2][C3]. The module view is a 5 - Stressed score with Medium confidence, because the pack has one set of company documents and a single dealer file.

Leverage is 8.44x net on SSIM EBITDA (calc: net leverage = 1,638 / 194 = 8.44x), with the revolver fully drawn [C7]. Revenue fell 10.6% and EBITDA 25.0% in the first half of 2026 (calc: H1 2026 revenue change = (676 - 756) / 756 * 100 = -10.6), which is operating deleverage in action [C13]. Free cash flow is -67 LTM (calc: LTM free cash flow = (-21) - 46 = -67), against cash of 62 [C6].

The covenant and payment events make time the binding constraint: first-lien net leverage is 8.03x against 6.50x, the equity cure window closes on 19 October and the notes' grace period ends on 15 October [C10][C9]. The sponsor holds 88% and has committed nothing, and the landlord can block any path through the master lease [C12].

What would change the view: a funded equity cure with a standstill from the notes holders, evidence that Gulf Coast has stabilised, or a lessor concession on rent would move the direction to Stable; a lapsed grace period or a failed cure would move it to a filing case.

CP-2A.analysis_md:
The first thing to break under stress is the notes' grace period on 15 October 2026, followed within weeks by the cross-defaults that link the credit agreement and the master lease (P1, P3) [C3]. Of the quantified shocks, the largest is Adjusted EBITDA 10% below forecast at -16.8 of 12-month liquidity [C2], followed by a 100 bps rise in Term SOFR on 1,500 of floating debt at -15.0. Module view: Gulf Coast revenue and EBITDA misses matter more than rates, but time matters most. Confidence is Medium.

Six paths are listed with probability and impact. P1 (default on the notes) and P5 (the 2028 maturities) both carry High impact because they put 1,700 and 1,250 of debt in play [C6]. The Gulf Coast path (P2) is the most likely to arrive first because that segment is 48.5% of revenue and falling [C5].

The only sizeable mitigant is capex: cutting 25% of maintenance capex adds 10.0 of liquidity [C2]. It cannot offset an EBITDA miss and risks revenue. Triggers T1 to T4 give the early warnings.

CP-4.analysis_md:
The provisions weaken creditors most through amendment and asset-transfer capacity, and protect them least where it now matters. The first-lien springing test is Breached: net leverage is 8.03x against 6.50x (calc: first-lien net leverage = 1,188 / 148 = 8.03x) [C1][C7][C8]. Covenant EBITDA is 148 because the credit agreement deducts cash rent [C5]; the minimum liquidity floor of 50 is Tight with 12 of headroom (calc: liquidity headroom = 62 - 50 = 12) [C9].

The sponsor's equity cure is available once and needs 34.8 of deemed EBITDA (calc: EBITDA cure = 1,188 / 6.5 - 148 = 34.8); a funded cure buys one quarter and does not reduce debt. Three terms make the PD/LGD picture worse: the unrestricted-subsidiary basket of 120 with no leverage test, open-market purchases that need not be offered to all lenders, and amendments of priority at 50.1% [C3]. Free-and-clear capacity of 118.4 falls 31.6 short of the sponsor's 150 priming proposal, so the proposal relies on a majority-lender amendment (calc: sponsor proposal beyond the free-and-clear basket = 150 - 118.4 = 31.6) [C2].

Module view: the documents give the borrower more room than the lenders to reshape the structure, and the lessor's cross-default adds a third party with a veto. Confidence is Medium because the summaries in the pack are not the executed documents.

CP-2H.analysis_md:
The pack cannot say which rating trigger is nearest or when, so this module is Blocked. What is evidenced is the pressure itself: Moody's lowered the corporate family rating to Caa2 from Caa1 on 2026-07-21, and S&P lowered the issuer credit rating to CCC from CCC+ on 2026-08-04, both with negative outlooks [C1].

No agency report was admitted to the Source Pack, so the agencies' stated downgrade thresholds, their leverage and coverage metrics and any timing language are unknown. Without them there is no threshold against which to compute headroom, and inventing one would present a guess as an extraction. The trigger and migration tables therefore keep their rows and leave every value blank.

As an analyst view, not an extraction: both agencies typically move to a default-category rating when a coupon is unpaid beyond its grace period. If the 15 October 2026 grace period lapses the next action is probably a downgrade to default, which would be a trigger event for any rating-linked covenants and investor mandates. Confidence in this module is not assessed.

- Rating triggers (downgrade and upgrade thresholds, metrics, current and projected values, headroom): no rating-agency report admitted, so the thresholds are unknown. Effect: no rating-trigger headroom or bullet chart values. Lifted by: a Moody's or S&P rating report or press release.
- Migration timing and catalysts: no agency commentary admitted. Effect: the likely transition and earliest timing are blank for both agencies and both cases. Lifted by: the same reports.
- Cites: the ratings themselves are cited in CP-1A's ratings register and in this module's analysis; the table rows cite nothing because they contain no extracted value.

CP-3D.analysis_md:
The market is pricing a high chance of default and heavy losses across the structure: the first-lien loan at 74 implies a 75.7% three-year default probability and a loss of 26.5% (calc: 3-year cumulative default probability = (1 - (1 - 0.3763) * (1 - 0.3763) * (1 - 0.3763)) * 100 = 75.7%), and the unsecured notes at 23 imply 92.4% and a loss of 83.2% [C1][C2]. The levels are consistent with the Caa2 / CCC corporate ratings and negative outlooks recorded in CP-1A [C5]. Module view: the quotes are Current (1 October 2026) but are single-dealer, so they are indicative, not tradable. Confidence is Medium-Low.

Loan levels translate to a three-year discount margin of 1,317 bps for the first lien and 2,817 bps for the second lien; the notes yield 55.7% and trade 5,180 bps over the three-year reference [C4]. The first and second lien imply almost the same hazard rate (37.6% and 37.6% a year), which is consistent: the market prices the same default event and differs only in recoveries.

Against the fundamentals the market is more bearish than the analyst on the first lien and more hopeful on the notes. What remains unpriced is the sponsor's priming proposal, which would move value from the existing first lien to new money.

- Single dealer: only one dealer file is in the pack. Effect: quotes are not corroborated and bid-ask is not shown here. Lifted by: a second dealer or TRACE-type prints.
- Recovery assumptions: the 65%, 25% and 10% are market-convention inputs, not extracted. Effect: the implied PD scales with them. Lifted by: the recovery waterfall in CP-4C.

CP-3C.analysis_md:
Refinancing pressure is concentrated in 2028, when 1,234.25 falls due (the revolver on 15 March and the term loan B on 30 September) against no projected source, a gap of 1,234.25 [C1][C2]. The earlier years are small: 5.25 in 2026 and 10.50 in 2027, but even these are unfunded from 2027 because the base case has no cash left. The most credible route is an amend-and-extend with an uptier in the short run and a pre-packaged Chapter 11 as the end state. Confidence is Medium.

The documents make the uptier executable: 120 of unrestricted-subsidiary investment capacity, non-pro-rata open-market purchases and 50.1% amendments [C4][C5]. The 150 sponsor proposal exceeds free-and-clear capacity of 118.4, so it needs a majority amendment [C6].

Creditor exposure splits by class and case. In the base case the second lien loses 133.5 and the notes 200; in the stress case the first lien itself loses 223; and a 150 priming loan takes the first-lien loss from 0 to 33.5 while leaving the junior classes unchanged.

- Sponsor intent on equity: only the priming proposal is evidenced. Lifted by: sponsor correspondence.

CP-4C.analysis_md:
The distress gate is Met: the coupon on the notes is unpaid inside its grace period, the covenant is breached and liquidity covers less than 12 months of mandatory uses [C1][C2]. The most credible path is a pre-packaged Chapter 11, with an amend-and-extend with an uptier as the sponsor's first try. In the base case (7.25x of SSIM EBITDA, EV 1,406.5) the fulcrum is the second lien, recovering 46.6%; in the stress case the fulcrum is the first lien at 82.2% [C5]. Confidence is Medium-Low, because the EV rests on analyst multiples.

Recoveries by class: first lien 100% base, 82.2% stress; second lien 46.6% base and 100% in the high case; notes 0% base and 54.5% high (the notes are the fulcrum there). The liquidation case, at 708, leaves the first lien with 53.4% [C6].

Weighted 30/50/10/10 across stress, base, high and liquidation [C7], the expected recoveries are 90.0% on the first lien, 33.3% on the second lien and 5.5% on the notes (calc: expected recovery of C3-2L = (30 * 0 + 50 * 46.6 + 10 * 100 + 10 * 0) / 100 = 33.3%). Against dealer prices of 74, 41 and 23, the market is more bearish than this view on the first lien and more hopeful on the notes.

The master lease is assumed rather than rejected in every scenario, so rent is an operating cost and the landlord is not in the waterfall; a rejection claim would reduce every recovery. A 150 priming loan would take its full amount off the value available to the existing classes [C8].
CP-4C.gaps_md:
- Independent valuation: none; the multiples are analyst-set. Effect: every recovery moves one-for-one with EV. Lifted by: an adviser's valuation.
- Master-lease treatment: assumed rather than rejected; no lessor term sheet. Effect: a rejection claim would be additional and senior in practice. Lifted by: the landlord's position.
- Intercreditor and plan mechanics: not in the pack; classes are assumed to follow strict priority.

CP-3.analysis_md:
The first-lien term loan B at 74 is the best-compensated existing instrument: its probability-weighted recovery is 90.0% (calc: expected recovery of C2-1L = (30 * 82.2 + 50 * 100 + 10 * 100 + 10 * 53.4) / 100 = 90.0%), 16.0 points above the price (calc: expected recovery above price = 90 - 74 = 16.0), while the second lien at 41 is worth 33.3% and the notes at 23 are worth 5.5% [C1]. The new-money first-out loan at talk of S+950-1,050 with a 96 OID implies a 3-year discount margin of 1,083 to 1,183 bps, inside the existing term loan B at 1,317 bps despite ranking ahead of it (calc: implied 3-year DM at mid talk = 1,000 + (100 - 96) / 3 * 100 = 1,133) [C4]. Module view: the term loan B is preferred among the existing debt and the new money looks attractive at talk, but the talk is not a market level. Confidence is Medium-Low.

The Valuations are V3 - Fair for the term loan B and second lien and V4 - Unattractive for the notes, because the notes price on the option value of the high case and the second lien at 41 pays for upside the scenarios do not give it. Dealer quotes are from one file dated 1 October 2026 and are Current [C2].

The relative-value blocks place the Larchmere loan against a CCC loan index at 72.5 and two synthetic loan peers at 78.5 and 69.0, and the notes against a CCC high-yield index at 64 and two synthetic bonds at 52 and 37 [C5]. Larchmere's notes at 23 are the cheapest and the weakest in the set.
CP-3.gaps_md:
- Talk is not a market level: NEW-1 has no commitment papers, so its Valuation is conditional. Lifted by: final terms from the sponsor.
- Revolver: no quote exists for the fully drawn revolver, so no priced row is shown.
- Peers: the index levels and Peers C to F are synthetic; they are labelled and not traced to a vendor file.

CP-5.analysis_md:
The analysis is traceable enough for a screening-level stance and not for committing capital. 17 upstream handoffs were checked: 2 Pass, 14 Restricted and 1 Blocked (CP-2H). In this design run every figure cites a labelled synthetic input; in a live run the same table would resolve to pack files. The provenance gap that matters most is the missing rating-agency report: ratings are evidenced only by a market file [C1] and the trigger thresholds are untraceable.

The second gap is valuation: every recovery moves one-for-one with an analyst multiple because no independent valuation was admitted, so the fulcrum conclusion is conditional. The third is market evidence from a single dealer.

Four findings are recorded: two open (agency report, single dealer) and two accepted (the labelled covenant-EBITDA definition and the half-year overstatement in the first projected year). Confidence is Medium.

CP-6.analysis_md:
The recommendation that survives the strongest challenge is 3 - MW on the first-lien loan, 4 - Modest UW on the second lien, 5 - Strong UW on the notes, and Avoid for the Fenwick Park CLO. The CLO book holds 2.80% of NAV in the first-lien loan against a 2.5% Hard single-issuer limit, so Portfolio Fit is Breaches and caps the final at Avoid [C7].

By Strategy the uncapped views are CLO 3 - MW, Indexed Loans 3 - MW and Indexed HY 5 - Strong UW. The decision rests on expected recoveries of 90.0%, 33.3% and 5.5% by class against prices of 74, 41 and 23 [C6][C3].

The strongest challenge is the sponsor's priming proposal: 150 of first-out money would rank ahead of every existing class [C4]. It is why the first lien is MW and not overweight. Catalysts begin on 15 October. Confidence is Medium-Low; the decision is conditional on the analyst-set enterprise values.
CP-6.gaps_md:
- Position sizing: not part of the Recommendation; the CLO book's maximum size for the loan is zero under the Fit result.
- Independent valuation and agency thresholds: not in the pack (CP-4C and CP-2H); both condition the view.
